antiphona-i: His disciples said * unto Blessed Martin: Father, why wilt thou go away from us? or with whom wilt thou leave us orphans? For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.
antiphona-ii: Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not * to work. thy will be done.
antiphona-iii: Not to be told is this man's glory; * whom work did not and death could not conquer; who neither feared to die, nor refused to live.
antiphona-iv: With eyes and hands lifted up to heaven, * he never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer. Alleluia.
antiphona-v: Martin is called joyfully into Abraham's bosom. * Martin, who was poor here and of small estimation, entereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.

datum: O how blessed a man is he! * His soul hath entered into possession in Paradise. There the Angels cry aloud for joy, there the Archangels make glad, there the whole company of the Saints do shout, there the army of the Virgins do call others to follow, (saying:) Make thine everlasting abode with us.

Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that the worshipful Feast of thy blessed Confessor and Bishop Martin, may avail us to the increase both of godliness toward thee, and healthfulness to our own souls.
For the testimony of blessed Martin, * let us praise our God.

antiphona-i: While Martin * is yet a Catechumen, he hath clad Me in this garment.
antiphona-ii: Martin * confessed the faith of the Holy Trinity, and received the grace of baptism.
antiphona-iii: Not * in the shelter of a buckler, nor of an helmet, but with the sign of the Cross will I pierce the hosts of the enemy.

incipit: This is that Martin whom God chose to be an High Priest unto Himself, he upon whom the Lord was pleased to bestow favour like as upon His Apostles;
responsum: So that he prevailed gloriously in the power of the Divine Trinity three times to raise the dead to life.
versus: Martin confessed the faith of the Holy Trinity.

incipit: Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work for them.
versus: With eyes and hands lifted up to heaven, he never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer.

incipit: Oh, how blessed a man was Bishop Martin!
responsum: He neither feared to die, nor refused to live.
versus: Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work for them. thy will be done.

antiphona-i: I trust * in the Lord that at thy prayers my daughter shall be healed.
antiphona-ii: When Tetradius * knew the power of God, he attained unto the grace of baptism.
antiphona-iii: Not to be told * is this man's glory, by whom so many wonderful works have been set forth before us!

lectio-i: Martin was born at Sabaria in Pannonia. When he was ten years old he went to the Church, in the spite of his (heathen) father and mother, and by his own will was numbered among the Catechumens. At fifteen years of age he joined the army, and served as a soldier first under Constantius and then under Julian. Once at the gate of Amiens a poor man asked him for an alms for Christ's name's sake, and since he had nothing to his hand but his arms and his clothes, he gave him half of his cloak. In the night following Christ appeared to him clad in the half of his cloak, and saying (to the angels who bare Him company) While Martin is yet a Catechumen, he hath clad Me in this garment.
lectio-ii: At eighteen years of age he was baptized. He gave up thereupon the life of a soldier, and betook himself to Hilary, Bishop of Poietiers, by whom he was placed in the order of Acolytes. Being afterwards made Bishop of Tours, he built a monastery wherein he lived in holiness for a while in company of four-score monks. At the last he fell sick of a grievous fever at Cande, a village in his diocese, and besought God in constant prayer to set him free from the prison of this dying body. His disciples heard him and said Father, why wilt thou go away from us? unto whom wilt thou bequeath us in our sorrow? Their words moved Martin, and he said Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work.
lectio-iii: When his disciples saw him, in the height of the fever, lying upon his back and praying, they entreated him to turn over and take a little rest upon his side while the violence of his sickness would allow him. But Martin answered them Suffer me to look heavenward rather than earthward, that my spirit may see the way whereby it is so soon going to the Lord. At the moment of death he saw the enemy of mankind, and cried out: What are you come here for, you bloody brute? You murderer, you'll find nothing in me. With these words on his lips, he gave up his soul to God, being aged eighty years. He was received by a company of Angels, who were heard praising God by many persons, especially by holy Severinus, Bishop of Cologne.

incipit: With eyes and hands lifted up to heaven
responsum: He never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer.
versus: While as blessed Martin was offering up the mysteries, a ball of fire appeared above his head.

incipit: Blessed Martin knew of his own death of a long time before it came to pass, and he said unto the brethren:
responsum: That the dissolution of his body was nigh at hand, for he deemed himself to be already breaking up.
versus: His bodily strength gave way all of a sudden, and he called his disciples together, and said unto them

incipit: His disciples said unto blessed Martin: Father, why wilt thou go away from us, and with whom wilt thou leave us orphans?
responsum: For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.
versus: We know that thou wouldest fain be with Christ, but, sooner or later, thy reward is sure. Rather, then, have pity upon us, whom thou art leaving.

datum: The Lord Jesus Christ * said not that He would come clothed in purple or adorned with a crown.
O Martin, * thou Priest of God, the heavens are open unto thee, yea, and the kingdom of My Father.
O Martin, * thou Priest of God, thou worthy shepherd, pray God on our behalf.

lectio-i: A Lesson from the Holy Gospel according to Luke.

In that time: Jesus said to his disciples: No man lighteth a candle, and putteth it in a hidden place, nor under a bushel; but upon a candlestick, that they that come in, may see the light. And so on.

In that which goeth before, Christ hath set the Church before the synagogue, and He exhorteth us rather to trust in the Church. The candle is faith, even as it is written thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path. (Ps. cxviii. 105.) Our faith is the word of God. The word of God is light. Faith is the candle. It is written concerning the Word of God, that That was the true Light, Which lighteth every man that cometh into this world. (John i. 9.) But a candle cannot shine, unless it be lighted from some other fire.

incipit: Blessed indeed was this man, at the time of whose passing the Saints sang in company, a band of Angels shouted aloud for joy
responsum: And an army of all the Powers of heaven came out to meet him, singing praises.
versus: His strength is a stay to the Church, his manifestation a glory to the Priests of God; Michael and his Angels took him away.

incipit: Martin was carried joyfully into Abraham's bosom. Martin, who was poor here and of small estimation,
responsum: Etereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.
versus: Bishop Martin, that jewel of Priests, goeth away from time, liveth in Christ.

datum: O how blessed a Bishop was he! * All his bowels yearned on the King Christ, and he had no dread for the power of the Empire! O how holy a soul was his, which passed not away by the sword of the persecutor, and yet lost not the palm of martyrdom.
